Before voting on 4853

Proposal 4853 would appoint a temporary supervisor to investigate the Phoenix Foundation’s board dispute and seek powers that could lead to a director’s removal.

The four concerns below cover who approved payments, which contract powers transferred, whether funded work was accepted, and a failed proposal to reduce the votes needed for board approval.

Read the four concerns What passing 4853 changes

This review does not recommend YES, NO or anyone’s removal.

What if the ampLUNA hub voted YES?

Four concerns in the records

0xphilipp helped approve releases from ERIS’s Creda grant

0xphilipp proposed and voted YES on A209, enabling 200,000 USDC for Creda’s first three milestones. Vini and MB supplied the other two YES votes. A215 later enabled another 10,000 USDC for analytics, bringing the grant total to 210,000 USDC.

Both were three-director approvals. The Treasury action marks all four milestones claimed. These amounts funded the project; they do not establish personal profit or independent acceptance of the work.

Creda’s grant, approval votes and milestones

The handover left some contract powers unchanged

ERIS proposal 9 gave the Phoenix board upgrade control over two contracts. The hub’s internal owner and the ICS20 contract’s internal governance setting did not change. Other Treasury and TLA permissions also remain.

A contract’s upgrade administrator and its internal owner can have different powers. The records identify authorized addresses; they do not establish who holds every key.

Which powers transferred and which remain

Payment records do not show acceptance of every milestone

Phoenix grants identified for Creda, Votion and the migration app total 265,000 USDC. Transfers and claimed milestones are recorded; independent acceptance of every deliverable has not been established.

AADAO separately reports Votion’s Hydro work complete and jointly verified. Project funding is not personal profit, and a later unfinished page does not prove that no work occurred.

Funding, delivered work and missing acceptance records

A272 proposed concentrating board approval power

A272 proposed removing Vini and lowering the approval threshold to 60%, allowing two of the remaining three seats to approve an action. It failed: 0xphilipp and MB voted YES, Rose voted NO and Vini was absent.

The board remained four seats with a 75% threshold. 4853 now seeks a supervisor and removal-facilitation powers over the same dispute. A later removal and threshold change could reopen the concentration risk; neither happens automatically on passage.

The route from failed A272 to proposal 4853

Could the hub change the vote?

In the 27 October snapshot, a full YES vote from the ampLUNA hub would raise YES from 40.00% to 53.59% of non-abstain votes, changing the result from failing to passing if nothing else changed.

The hub had not voted, and its vAMP gauge had no recorded votes. Validators voted differently: Smart Stake and Ceres chose VETO; HighStakes chose ABSTAIN. The calculation shows potential voting power, not a voting agreement.

Before the vote closes

  1. Disclose financial interests

    Directors, Think Tank members, validators and contractors should disclose relevant payments, grants, hosting arrangements and voting interests under their public role or handle.

    Who has which role

  2. Publish voting instructions

    Explain planned hub and gauge votes. Where a validator follows a DAO mandate, finish the internal vote first. Lion DAO’s validator changed to YES while its A33 vote was still open.

    Lion DAO’s voting sequence

  3. Provide the missing approval records

    Publish recusal decisions, milestone acceptance, contract handover terms and any approved extensions. Retain the ballots, payment records and responses for independent review.

    Proposed governance changes

Check the sources

The source library includes ballot exports, transaction responses and calculation files. The 27 October supplement checked 48 successful transactions, including 38 Terra transaction-byte hashes. Six cited transactions remain unavailable. This is not an independent audit of every transaction.
